rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded blastocyst and visible ICM, but the TE is not clearly assessable as uniformly AA from this single image and some described details (e.g., circumferential cohesive epithelium, minimal fragmentation) are somewhat overcalled.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, prior ectopic, diagnosis, and semen data well with embryo quality, though some links (stress, moderate alcohol, partner age 36) are somewhat overstated.

The structure is logical and the prognosis estimate broadly follows from embryo quality and patient factors, but the additive percentage adjustments are somewhat arbitrary and a few risk deductions are not strongly evidence-based.

Mostly aligned on embryo grading, prognosis framing, and ectopic surveillance, but recommendations such as routine aspirin, thrombophilia testing for ectopic history, NK cell testing, and ERA/EMMA/ALICE after a single failure are not well supported by major guidelines.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer monitoring and contingency planning, though several suggested investigations/interventions are more aggressive than typically indicated for this case.
